findings.title: REPLACENODE issued during scale-down when < 2 nodes are live → opaque 400 → eviction livelock
findings.scenario: S4 (admin call issued before its Solr-side precondition holds; composes with S2 opaque-v1-error)
findings.summary: During a scale-down of TargetNode, transient ZK session loss can reduce Solr's live_nodes to just the target itself while a still-lagged CLUSTERSTATUS shows the target holding replicas. The operator issues REPLACENODE (sourceNode=target) with only a podHasReplicas guard and no live-target check (solr_update_util.go:569-582). Solr's handler rejects it with HTTP 400 because getLiveNodes().size() <= 1 (ReplaceNodeCmd.java:62-67). The v1 client collapses every StatusCode>=400 into an opaque ServiceUnavailable, discarding the error body (api.go:173-176), so the operator cannot tell a semantic 400 from a transient 503. The non-nil error leaves canDeletePod=false with the ScaleDown lock retained, so level-triggered reconciliation re-submits the identical impossible REPLACENODE forever — a livelock that never completes and never surfaces a terminal failure until ≥2 nodes are live again. This is a new precondition-livelock beyond the three known-good-grounding bugs.
